summary: Italy supports renewables through two-way Contracts for Difference run by the state energy agency GSE, under the FER 2 and FER X decrees, and profits move freely. Permitting and tension between national and regional rules are the main risks.

access.reason: Support is allocated through GSE schemes, FER 2 for innovative technologies from June 2024 and the transitional FER X from December 2024.

terms.reason: Larger plants receive two-way Contracts for Difference, and plants below 300 kW receive an all-inclusive tariff.

buyer.reason: Payments come from GSE, a state-controlled body.

ownership.reason: There are no restrictions on currency transfers, and profits can be freely repatriated.

build.reason: Permitting remains a significant issue despite simplification, and landscape and heritage constraints can block plants.

stability.reason: Tension between national and regional rules creates legal uncertainty for developers.

direction.reason: FER X and FER 2 opened new support rounds in 2024, and permitting has been simplified.

access.reason: Self-consumption rules were updated recently, alongside simplified authorisation for smaller plants.

ownership.reason: No restrictions on currency transfers or repatriating profits.

build.reason: Permitting and regional rules remain the main barriers.

direction.reason: No major change to self-consumption rules was found after 2024.

sources.title: Italy Country Commercial Guide, trade financing

gaps: Contract length, grid connection times and corporate PPA practice were not covered by the sources reviewed.
